correctness.rationale: Arbitrary one-coordinate antiderivative generator tests give all three conditional transfer laws. Stationarity of \((x^2+y^2)/2\), \((x^2-y^2)/2\), and \(z^2/2\) gives a two-by-two linear system for the transverse wave energies, yielding \(\nu_1\mathbb E[x^2]=hm-q\) and \(\nu_2\mathbb E[y^2]=hm+q\). Subtracting the square of the mean gives the exact pump-height shell. If \(\mathbb E[x^2]=0\), bounded complete support dynamics successively forces \(x=y=z=0\), so every non-origin state has strict defect. Jensen then gives \(0<m<h\), and the negative expectation of \(z(z-h)\) forces positive mass in \(0<z<h\). The packaged checker verifies the polynomial and moment algebra exactly.

value.rationale: The parameter h is the physical pumping amplitude of the three-wave interaction, so the interval \(0<z<h\) and the parabola \(m(h-m)\) are intrinsic to the source model rather than arbitrary statistics. The theorem reduces both transverse wave energies exactly to the first two moments of the third wave and identifies the gap from the pump-height parabola with the first wave's mean-square amplitude. It also proves that every nontrivial compact recurrent state must place positive invariant mass inside the pump-selected height slab. The fiberwise transfer laws and coordinate-speed defects provide exact consistency checks for periodic, self-excited chaotic, and hidden-attractor statistics in a system whose modern literature emphasizes the difficulty of distinguishing sustained from very long transient chaos numerically.
